desc: The only federal court case in which a US agency has been held to have failed its search obligations on UFO-related records. Leslie Kean, represented by Lobel, Novins & Lamont (Martin Lobel, Lee Ellen Helfrich), sued the National Aeronautics and Space Administration on 9 December 2003 in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia over NASA's handling of her 31 January 2003 FOIA request for records referring to Kecksburg, the 9 December 1965 incident, the 'Fragology Files' for 1962-1967, Richard M. Schulherr, Project Moon Dust and Cosmos 96. The case was assigned to Judge Emmet G. Sullivan, cause code '05:552 Freedom of Information Act', PACER case ID 106063. NASA ran four searches. The court's 27 March 2007 memorandum opinion records that 'plaintiff contends, and indeed NASA admits, that NASA's first two searches for responsive documents were inadequate', traces how a granted administrative appeal signed by Associate Deputy Administrator James Jennings on 18 June 2003 was simply not acted on because of poor tracking and an office move, and holds that NASA 'has not yet met its burden of demonstrating that the search for documents was adequate.' Summary judgment was granted to NASA only on the withholding of two emails between FOIA officer Stephen McConnell and NASA attorney Bierbower under Exemption 5, which the court reviewed in camera on its own 22 February 2007 order. The court then ordered the parties to propose search and documentation procedures that would create a proper record. A Stipulation of Settlement in Part was signed by Judge Sullivan on 16 October 2007; NASA searched under supervision and filed joint status reports every sixty days from December 2007 to August 2009; the case was dismissed on 24 August 2009 on the parties' joint motion, the court finding NASA had met its settlement obligations. Along the way, NASA public liaison officer Steve McConnell testified that two boxes of papers from the period of the Kecksburg incident were missing.

entityInfo.desc: The only federal court finding in existence that a US agency failed its records-search obligations on a UFO matter. Docket 1:03-cv-02509 (D.D.C.), Judge Emmet G. Sullivan, filed 9 December 2003, dismissed 24 August 2009 after a court-supervised re-search under a stipulated settlement. The opinion's most quotable line for this domain is not about UFOs at all: 'Plaintiff contends, and indeed NASA admits, that NASA's first two searches for responsive documents were inadequate.' The template - request, appeal, sue, obtain a supervised search, litigate status reports for two years - is the only method that has ever forced a US agency to look again.

timeline.label: Kean's FOIA request
timeline.text: Leslie Kean files with NASA for records on Kecksburg, the 9 December 1965 incident, the Fragology Files 1962-1967, Richard M. Schulherr, Project Moon Dust and Cosmos 96. NASA answers 'no records' on 11 April 2003.

timeline.label: Kean v. NASA filed
timeline.text: Thirty-eight years to the day after Kecksburg, Kean sues NASA in the District of Columbia. The case is assigned to Judge Emmet G. Sullivan.

timeline.label: Court finds NASA's searches inadequate
timeline.text: Judge Sullivan holds that NASA 'has not yet met its burden of demonstrating that the search for documents was adequate', denies summary judgment in part, and orders the parties to propose search and documentation procedures creating a proper record. NASA had already admitted its first two searches were inadequate.

timeline.label: Stipulated settlement in part
timeline.text: Judge Sullivan signs the Stipulation of Settlement in Part and orders joint status reports every sixty days. NASA searches under court supervision for the next twenty-two months.

timeline.label: Kean v. NASA dismissed
timeline.text: On the parties' joint motion and NASA's representation that it had met its settlement obligations, the case is dismissed. The only federal finding of an inadequate UFO-related records search stands undisturbed.
